rationale: A wins because it separates the real stories instead of chasing the shiniest anxiety. A's "Replit will tell you it builds working apps — it won't tell you how often they actually work" is a clean reporter-shaped tension with the missing proof named; B's "Replit's new agent lets non-coders spin up live databases. Who's checking what's in them?" is catchy, but it starts building a security story the facts have not earned. B has instincts, but A has discipline, and discipline is what keeps a founder out of a reporter's trash folder.
gaps_in_A: "from one English sentence" overstates the supplied fact. The update says a plain-English description, not one sentence.
"You pay per build" invents the billing unit. The facts only say usage-based pricing on top of subscriptions; A later admits it does not know whether the unit is "per build? per deploy? per token?"

"Can a student who can't code now ship a real app?" is a fair education hook, but it leans ahead of the evidence. The update says Replit is used heavily in education, not that the new agent is already used in classrooms.

The set uses "end-to-end" as shorthand for the product claim. It is accurate enough here, but it is still on the slop blacklist and should be replaced with the actual sequence: code, database, deploy.
gaps_in_B: "huge, largely non-technical user base" is not in the update. Replit has tens of millions of users and is targeting non-engineers with this agent; that does not prove the existing user base is largely non-technical.
"betting its core product" is an invented strategic claim. The facts support a launch, not a company-wide bet.

"a larger on-ramp for unreviewed data infrastructure showing up inside organizations and schools" turns a database-setup fact into a shadow-IT/security premise without evidence of organizational deployment, misconfiguration, or data exposure.

"Replit's usage-based pricing shows where AI agent costs are headed" being refused as "duplicate" is a bad call. Pricing is a distinct software-business angle if Replit can provide actual rates and usage examples.
